claims.statement: The repository's verification is split across three layers: JVM unit tests (JUnit 4, no device needed) are the primary gate for all planner/resolver/facade/repository logic; `:app:connectedAndroidTest` runs Compose UI instrumentation tests (HomeScreen/PlaylistScreen/SettingsScreen compose tests) requiring a device; and `:benchmark:connectedCheck` runs macrobenchmarks (StartupBenchmark cold-start with 5 iterations, ScrollBenchmark, BaselineProfileGenerator) that also regenerate the Baseline Profile shipped in release builds.

The `check` lifecycle task aggregates the root `spotlessCheck`, the root `verifyProductArchitecture` task, and every subproject's `check` (each of which runs that module's unit tests and its own spotlessCheck), so a `check` failure may originate from formatting, an architecture assertion, or a unit test and must be diagnosed from the GradleException message.

The mood time-slot feature's design doc §7 (item 7) defines a regression floor: with the enhancement switch off, lucky-play behavior must remain bit-for-bit identical to the pre-enhancement behavior, and the existing RandomQueuePlanner tests must not be modified and must stay green. UniformRandomPlannerTest and the non-mood PlayerRandomQueueFacadeTest cases (plus moodFilterDisabledKeepsOriginalBehavior / moodFilterInactiveOutsideSlotTime) carry the same baseline; mood filtering is therefore only allowed at the candidate-pool entrance in PlayerRandomQueueFacade, never inside the planners.

RandomQueuePlannerTest locks the lucky-play plan semantics: recently played songs are excluded and selections are merged into the recent set; when the remaining pool is smaller than the batch the history is cleared and resetHistory=true is reported; with uniform random enabled the low-play-count songs are still selected after the recent filter; planInfiniteStart records only queued playable songs as coverage; planInfiniteRefill excludes songs already in the queue while keeping existing exclusions; and no-playable-songs returns null.

UniformRandomPlannerTest locks the play-count tiered preemption semantics: flag-off degenerates to the injected shuffle; when enabled, songs are dynamically tiered by raw play count with lowest tiers preempting quota (a sufficient lower tier is never crossed, an insufficient one is fully taken then topped up), tiering stays effective when all counts exceed any fixed threshold because thresholds derive from the distribution, equal counts degrade to pure shuffle, orderSongs groups by count and shuffles within each group, and buildPlayOrderIds keeps the current song first for SHUFFLE mode while tiering the rest.

MoodSlotResolverTest locks all edge cases of time-slot resolution and validation: half-open [start, end) intervals (start minute hits, end minute does not), overnight slots with end <= start, at-most-one hit per minute across the full day for valid configs with deterministic earliest-start resolution for invalid overlaps, disabled switch or empty configs never activate, validation error classes (blank/overlong name > NAME_MAX_LENGTH=20, no tags, zero length, overlap returning Conflict naming the conflicting slot, touching slots allowed, same-id edit without self-conflict), and circular-overlaps semantics (overnight x morning intersect, two overnight slots always intersect, full-day overlaps everything non-zero).

The mood group of PlayerRandomQueueFacadeTest locks the facade-side filtering and degradation: when a slot is hit the random pool is narrowed to songs carrying the slot's tags; an empty tagged pool falls back to full-library random with a 'fall back to full library' log rather than failing to start; inactive slot time or a disabled switch preserves the original behavior; and mood filtering composes with uniform random so tiered preemption still applies inside the filtered pool (0-play songs ranked ahead of 10-play songs).

Two same-named ControllerQueuePlannerTest classes lock complementary queue semantics. The :domain one locks playable-order expansion (null for empty queue, sequential order with requested start, REVERSE ordering, stable SHUFFLE via playOrderIds, skipping unplayable songs to the next playable). The :player one locks controller-plan semantics (remainingAfterStart tail detection, duplicate songs 1,2,2,3 preserved with occurrence-based start index, addSongAsNext yielding controller order 1,2,5,3, play-mode changes rebuilding order, all-unplayable returning null).

PlaybackWindowPlannerTest locks the window slice (DEFAULT_PREVIOUS_COUNT=20 / DEFAULT_NEXT_COUNT=50, clamped at queue start/end, window-local vs full-queue index mapping, REVERSE-mode windows in playback order), and ControllerWindowSynchronizerTest locks window caching (non-forced plans reuse the window but re-anchor startIndex to the current song, forced plans after addSongAsNext invalidate and recompute, empty queue returns null).

PlaybackWindowPerformanceShapeTest locks the product-level performance shape: for 100/500/1000-song queues the controller window stays <= 71 items and >= 51 items at start/middle/end, including a 1000-song stable-shuffle window that must not expand to the full queue. The file's existence and required terms ('100', '500', '1_000', '71', 'WindowedControllerQueuePlanner') are themselves machine-enforced by verifyProductArchitecture (whose rule body lives in buildSrc ProductArchitectureVerification), so deleting or renaming the file's required substrings fails the architecture gate.

MediaItemWrapDetectionTest locks index-based wrap detection (not transition-reason-based, because Media3 reports REPEAT_MODE_ALL tail wrap as SEEK): last-index-to-0 is a wrap, normal forward navigation, one-step previous, unknown previous (C.INDEX_UNSET), and non-zero new index are not; a 2-item window's backward move is treated as a wrap (harmless since the refill planner deduplicates); empty or single-item windows cannot wrap. The checked function is isMediaItemWrap(newIndex==0 && previous!=UNSET && previous>=count-1 && previous>newIndex).

SingleItemLoopRewindDetectionTest locks single-item loop rewind detection for REPEAT_MODE_ALL queues of exactly one item (0-to-0 transitions that never fire onMediaItemTransition and must be caught via AUTO discontinuity plus position rewind): with known duration the old position must be near the end, with unknown duration a conservative threshold applies and rewinds from under 30 seconds count as buffering jitter (LOOP_REWIND_MIN_POSITION_MS); SEEK-reason rewinds (manual drag to start) never count as completion (anti-abuse); multi-item queues, index changes, and non-zero new positions are rejected; threshold boundary values still detect. isSingleItemLoopRewind requires reason==AUTO_TRANSITION, mediaItemCount==1, oldIndex==0, newIndex==0, newPositionMs <= LOOP_REWIND_NEW_POSITION_MAX_MS, and the near-end condition.

ControllerPlaybackStateSynchronizerTest locks the Media3-snapshot-to-UI-state mapping: mediaId (Song.id.toString()) maps back to the business queue and updates currentIndex while emitting duration updates and playback-start events; unknown mediaId keeps the current song; already-tracked songs do not re-emit playback start; a pause during buffering is not treated as a real pause (isPlayingTransition three cases); and QueueManager.restorePlayModeAfterNextSong restores the pre-next play mode only for the relevant song with an injectable play-order builder.

PlaybackRestoreCoordinatorTest locks startup restore semantics: no stored state returns null; a missing or unplayable current song restores the queue but without a playable session; the normal path builds a playable session carrying the restore position and same-name song group sorted by sample rate descending; and the infinite-play flag with its played-song coverage set survives restore unchanged.

PlaybackStateStoreTest locks the DataStore-backed snapshot store: save/restore round-trips keep queue, currentIndex, mode, playOrderIds, duplicate items, and infinite-play state; restore filters songs that no longer exist; saveCurrentPlaybackSnapshot corrects index/position from the live current song and can even create a queue for a song that was not in the saved queue; an empty-session save (transient all-empty state during UI rebuild) must not erase an existing snapshot (2026-09-03 regression named in the test); an empty save with no prior snapshot writes nothing; an empty save carrying only a currentSongId keeps the existing queue but updates position, or restores a single-song queue when none existed (2026-10-06); and restore falls back to legacy SharedPreferences with the next successful save clearing the legacy keys.

PlaybackStateSnapshotSerializerTest locks snapshot JSON robustness: round-trips preserve duplicates, currentIndex, mode, and play order; damaged JSON and a missing required currentIndex decode to null rather than throwing; missing optional fields take defaults; and malformed or unavailable entries in infinitePlayedIds are silently dropped.

Each of the :feature:player facades has a same-named JVM test that uses fake callables to record side effects and locks the orchestration above the pure planners: PlayerQueueFacadeTest (setPlayQueue updates state and triggers persistence), PlayerControllerQueueFacadeTest (remainingMediaItems prefers controller info with a planned-queue fallback), PlayerMediaEventFacadeTest (tail/wrap triggers infinite refill only in infinite mode, restores play mode after add-next consuming the one-shot flag), PlayerPersistenceFacadeTest (async save captures the position before launching, and live-session restore skips the controller rebuild while still restoring the UI queue), and PlayerPlaybackStateAutosaverTest (immediate save then interval throttling with reset allowing the next immediate save).

NarrowFlowSyncTest and PlayerSleepTimerCoordinatorTest lock the 2026-09-03 narrow-flow regression baseline: discrete uiState updates must compare against the pre-update uiState old value so stale positions or zeroed sleep-timer countdowns are never flushed back into the narrow flows; true discrete position changes (seek), the restore path, and sleep-timer start must propagate to the narrow flow; and cancel must zero the countdown via the explicit resetSleepTimerNarrowFlow entry rather than value-diff propagation.

The :data repository tests run on the JVM without Android: Room repository tests exercise hand-written per-file FakeMelodyDao in-memory tables (MusicRepositoryRoomTest locks playlist cross-ref restore by sortOrder, orphan-ref filtering, duplicate-rejecting persistence, and titleOverride write/clear round-trips driving groupKey; PlayStatsRepositoryRoomTest locks incremental stat persistence, zero defaults for missing songs, and deterministic ranked ordering with raw-vs-effective count switching). :data explicitly adds the real org.json as a testImplementation because the Android SDK's org.json is a stub that throws on the JVM.

PlayerSettingsRepositoryTest locks settings persistence semantics using a real PreferenceDataStore over a temp file: defaults apply when nothing is stored (ThemeMode.SYSTEM, ThemeVariant.MONO, lyric font scale 1), and the legacy SharedPreferences fallback is one-shot — the first DataStore write also deletes the legacy key (asserted for both the dark-theme and global-uniform-random paths). PlaylistResumeDataStoreTest locks per-playlist resume record/overwrite/clear semantics.

The legacy migration tests lock the v1-JSON-to-Room path: LegacyJsonSnapshotParserTest locks parsing of songs/playlists/title overrides, play-stats pref prefixes (play_count_*, raw_play_count_*, play_duration_*), quick-skip songs and short-play counts, Chinese default values for missing optional fields, per-segment recovery from corrupt JSON, duplicate-URI dedup that keeps URI-less songs, and playlist refs restricted to migrated songs with reindexed sortOrder. SharedPreferencesLegacyJsonMigrationTest locks the one-shot orchestration: full data write plus a MigrationStateEntity completion marker, corrupt JSON still migrating stats and writing the marker, and an existing marker causing a complete skip with zero writes.

LrcParserOffsetTest locks the LRC [offset:] tag regression (2026-09-03 lyrics latency fix — the offset was previously discarded): a positive offset shifts all lyric timestamps earlier (timeMs += offset), a negative offset delays them, missing or non-numeric offsets keep original timestamps, the offset applies to every timestamp including multi-timestamp lines, and blank content returns null.

RuntimePermissionPolicyTest locks the version-gated permission specs: POST_NOTIFICATIONS is required only on API 33+ (TIRAMISU) and BLUETOOTH_CONNECT only on API 31+ (S), each returning a spec with its Chinese denied-message on qualifying versions and null below the threshold.

AppLoggerTest locks log redaction (content:// and file:// URIs, POSIX/Windows file paths, Bluetooth MAC addresses, and deviceName/bluetoothName fields are replaced with placeholders, including inside Throwable messages and stack traces), and PerformanceTraceTest locks the observability seam (measure passes through the block value, log output goes through AppLog with redacted metadata, release silence is governed by isEnabled, and allow/disallow whitelists named operations through to release builds). These tests back the architecture rule that forbids direct android.util.Log calls outside AppLogger.

SongEmotionSectionTest locks the emotion pure-function layer in :core:ui: smoothCurve keeps length and shrinks noise with short-list passthrough, lowConfidence marks the undetermined band (either axis |value| < 0.15), hasSignificantPeak requires an arousal spike standing out, the word table is closed (10 groups, 39 unique words with the ABYSS group at 3, headline as first word), per-window voting abstains on near-zero windows and takes up to MAX_TAGS groups by ratio, WITTY (鬼畜) is excluded from automatic voting (center-vacuum fix) while the manual groupOf path remains unrestricted, and emotionTagsOf gives user tags priority with empty output at low confidence.

Two small regression locks pin cross-cutting behaviors: ResolveResumeSongTest (app module) locks playlist-resume song resolution returning null when the resume is null, the song is absent from the playlist, or the song is unplayable under the injected/default (uri != null) rule; LyricsHighlightLeadTest (core:model) locks the lyric highlight lead (HIGHLIGHT_LEAD_MS) pre-scroll compensation — the upcoming line is highlighted ~300ms early by default, leadMs=0 preserves strict timestamp behavior, and negative lead delays highlight.

The project validation policy (AGENTS.md) prescribes the narrowest quiet validation: run the changed module's tests with --tests class filters before committing, reserve full `check` for pre-commit, and preserve complete failure output without truncation. verifyProductArchitecture failures name the offending file directly (e.g. PlaybackWindowPerformanceShapeTest must keep its required sizing terms, MusicRepository keeps its PerformanceTrace anchors). Gradle accepts multiple --tests filters in one invocation plus wildcard package patterns, and :benchmark:connectedCheck may fail on MIUI real devices due to ROM restrictions on macrobenchmark automation steps.

The v3.10.2 skin-description test suite (`core/skin`), read by the app-shell equivalence tests, locks the invariant that DefaultSkin.skin()'s built-in description equals today's app structure: 3 bottom tabs (曲库/播放/我的), player as a normal tab, a library page with exactly 4 segments (歌单/歌手/专辑/情绪) sourced from the `LibraryTab` enum, art size 44dp, and a player start route matching AppNavHost's original `startDestination = AppRoutes.HOME`.

SkinParserValidationTest locks fail-closed skin validation with precise typed reasons: non-JSON, missing/unsupported schema version (supported version `1` named in the message), unknown parts (fails closed, never silently degraded — even a real androidx widget not in the catalog), unknown icons, tab targeting a missing page, duplicate tab ids, a single-entry bottom bar, missing start page, invalid player entry / cover shape / row template / song-list source, and a segment without sections are all rejected by a specific `SkinIssue.Code`.

The skin iframe contract can express shells radically different from today (NetEase-style 3-tab card-wall with vinyl player, and a minimal 2-tab sheet-drawer skin), and the scope boundary is locked at L5/L6: all three built-in skins use only L1–L5 SkinPartCatalog parts and the catalog itself contains no L6/L7 entries. A `songList` part renders differently per template (`grid` vs `default`).

The app-shell suite in `:app` locks the built-in skeleton/section/template catalogs against the app structure as cross-module consistency (which module-boundary gates force into `:app`): AppShellEquivalenceTest verifies DefaultShell keeps the pre-refactor tabs/order/routes/mini-player rules; DefaultShellConsistencyTest asserts the Kotlin-constant shell and the skin-JSON-resolved shell match; SheetSkeletonTest proves the two-tab sheet-drawer shape assembles; SongListTemplateCatalogTest forces `SkinPartCatalog.SONG_LIST_TEMPLATES` to equal the `SongListTemplate` enum ids; SkinSwitcherCatalogConsistencyTest forces `UserSections.SKIN_SWITCHER` to equal `SkinPartCatalog.SKIN_SWITCHER`.

The library song-list row template maps from skin to Shell via LibrarySongListTemplateTest and GridLayoutSwitchTest: the default skeleton resolves to SongListTemplate.DEFAULT (zero visual change), a skeleton without a songList part falls back to DEFAULT, an unknown template is rejected fail-closed by the validator, and the global grid-layout switch forces GRID across all known skins while leaving the skin's own template untouched when off.

PlayerSettingsRepositoryTest verifies DataStore-backed settings persistence with a real PreferenceDataStoreFactory plus a fake SharedPreferences: defaults when nothing is stored (theme SYSTEM, variant MONO, lyric font scale 1, global uniform random on, Bluetooth monitoring off, playback notification off, daily listening goal 120 min), and per-key legacy fallback happens exactly once — the first DataStore write deletes the legacy key for theme, global uniform random, Bluetooth monitoring, and notification.

PlayerPlaybackStateAutosaverTest and PlayerSleepTimerCoordinatorTest lock narrow-flow persistence and timer regressions from the 2026-09-03 progress-bar rewind fix: the autosaver saves once immediately then throttles by interval and `reset` releases the next save; the sleep-timer coordinator writes countdown ticks only to the narrow flow (uiState.sleepTimerRemainingMs stays at its initial value) so cancel/fire resets must go through the explicit `resetRemainingMs`/`resetSleepTimerNarrowFlow` entry rather than a uiState value diff.

PlayerPersistenceGraphTest locks the restore handshake of PlayerPersistenceGraph (a site of four regressions, 4fdb2ae/0cce0de/53af2cc/2026-10-06): the controllerReady and pendingRestore flags converge in either order, a live session only refills the UI queue while an empty session fully restores, a connection failure fallback releases, and no snapshot means no restore; it uses Dispatchers.Unconfined so the graph's internal launch-io/withContext-main runs synchronously without a coroutines-test dependency. PlaybackStateStoreTest extends its snapshot semantics with the 2026-10-06 case that an empty save carrying only a currentSongId keeps the existing queue and updates position, or restores a single-song queue when none existed. Both persistence models also carry the isExplorePlay flag through snapshot save/restore so a killed process resumes into the same explore state.

The :feature:playlist SongListTemplateTest locks the L3 row-template enum: DEFAULT/GRID ids equal the catalog whitelist strings, fromId returns DEFAULT for unknown values in a fail-safe manner, and all template ids are distinct and non-blank; SongSelectionControllerTest locks the selection-controller state logic (case-insensitive title/artist filter, search toggle that clears the query, and multi-select enter/exit that manages the selected-id set).

LuckyPlayEntryPolicyTest locks the 「随心播放」 entry-bar policy shouldShowLuckyPlayEntry: shown on the sheet-drawer shell when no song is drawn, never shown while a song is playing (mutually exclusive with shouldShowMiniPlayer), and never shown on the tab shell because the player page already has the FAB — guarding inverted conditions, a missing SHEET limitation, and mini-player non-exclusion.

UserSectionsTest locks the me-page section keys and their order: the default order is 5 hardcoded items (userInfo, playStats, moodTimeSlot, emotionScan, fileCheck) plus an optional trailing skinSwitcher, all keys are distinct and non-blank, and UserSections.SKIN_SWITCHER equals the literal `skinSwitcher` so the page's recognized sections and the description's myOverview sections cannot drift apart.

ExplorePlaybackPolicy (pure :domain, no Android dependency) locks the explore skip-vs-complete judgment isSkipped(playedMs, durationMs): a song is counted as a quick skip when played < 30s or < 1/4 of its duration — a 4-min song played 20s is skipped, an 8-min song played 60s (>30s but <1/4=120s) is skipped, a 4-min song played 70s (>30s and >1/4=60s) is a full listen, and a short song fully played under 30s is still skipped. When duration <=0 (unknown) only the 30s rule applies. It also exposes the explore sizing constants INITIAL_BATCH_SIZE=10 and REFILL_COUNT=5.

WordPreferencesRepository locks the explore word-listening vote counting over the Room word_preferences table (word PRIMARY KEY, likeVotes, dislikeVotes, updatedAt): recordSongOutcome(votes: Map<String,Int>, liked=true) increments each word's likeVotes and recordSongOutcome(false) its dislikeVotes by the given per-word weight (the 80% dominant word weighs more than a 20% word; weights come from ExplorePlaybackPolicy.voteWeightOf). The writes are per-word atomic SQL increments (ensureWordPreference + addWordVotesDelta) with saturating MIN(x, 2147483647) math so two concurrent settles cannot lose votes (M-22 review replaces the old read-then-upsert-whole-table). Zero-weight and empty word lists are ignored, votes accumulate across sessions, and clearAll empties both the DAO table and the exposed map. The ownership decision (WordPreferenceKind) is deliberately NOT computed by the repository but by core/model WordPreference.kind (like>dislike LIKE, dislike>like DISLIKE, tie NEUTRAL), so a single skip never flips an already-liked word (votes only accumulate evidence).

MelodyDatabaseMigrationTest (Robolectric, sdk=34, MigrationTestHelper + imported schema export) locks the hand-written Room migrations from v1 through v17: runMigrationsAndValidate re-checks every step's resulting schema (tables/indices/PRIMARY KEY) against the target version's exported schema JSON so any hand-written SQL drifting from the @Entity definitions fails. Data-integrity cases insert old-shape rows before a step and assert survival/new-column defaults: 1→10 keeps inserted songs while filling per-version defaults (album NOT NULL DEFAULT '' from 3→4, durationMs NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 from 6→7, lrcUri nullable stays NULL from 2→3), 1→2 creates quick_skip_short_play_counts, 4→5 creates artists/albums/song_artist_cross_ref, 5→6 creates playback_events, 8→9 creates song_emotions and 9→10 adds the four personalization columns all-NULL, 10→11 creates the word_preferences table whose inserted row round-trips, 11→12 adds nullable userTagsEdited, 12→13 stamps the coordinate fingerprint and clears stale user coordinates, 14→15 restamps modelVersion to the v5 label without touching curves, 15→16 rescales all historical word votes ×100 to the weighted scale, and 16→17 adds the two missing indexes index_songs_albumId and index_playback_events_songId (verified via PRAGMA index_list with data survival).

The explore group of PlayerRandomQueueFacadeTest locks facade-side explore start and refill: under explore mode playRandomQueue produces exactly 10 songs, sets isExplorePlay, exits infinite mode (isInfinitePlay=false, cleared infinitePlayedSongIds) and logs 'explore=true'; an active explore session blocks startInfinitePlay (logs 'blocked by explore session') while a session that ended (user replaced the queue, isExplorePlay=false but mode still active) allows infinite again. refillExplorePlayQueue prefers songs carrying liked words only (no disliked words followed by no-liked-word fallback to the no-dislike pool logging 'no liked match', and full-library 'fall back to full library' when everything holds a disliked word), does nothing when not in an explore session, and uses startedSongId to correct the business-queue currentIndex so a stale index never syncs back to replay the just-ended song (2026-10-20 regression).

The explore group of PlayerMediaEventFacadeTest locks explore tail handling in handleMediaItemEnded: when the just-ended song was second-to-last (new remainingItems==0 after it becomes current) the facade settles the ended song via onExploreSongSettled(trackedSongId, playedMs) and triggers refillExplorePlayQueue; when the ended song was third-to-last (remainingItems==1) or the queue still has enough songs, no refill occurs (avoiding re-pull to replay); and a null tracked song skips the settle while still allowing the refill.

The explore sample tests of PlayerQueueFacadeTest lock the explore session lifecycle against manual queue operations: setPlayQueue (a user replacing the queue by tapping a playlist/top-hits) exits the explore session (isExplorePlay=false and isInfinitePlay=false), while merely calling addToPlayQueue (appending a song) keeps the explore session alive.

PlayerSettingsRepositoryTest's explore-mode settings (2026-10-20) lock the RandomEnhanceMode tri-state machine (OFF/TIME_SLOT/EXPLORE) over DataStore: nothing stored defaults to OFF; a legacy mood_time_slot_enabled=true without a new key falls back to TIME_SLOT; setRandomEnhanceMode(EXPLORE) writes RANDOM_ENHANCE_MODE=EXPLORE and syncs the legacy mood-time-slot switch to false (explore is not a time-slot mode) while setRandomEnhanceMode(TIME_SLOT) syncs it to true, so both the new key and the legacy switch read paths agree.

The emotion-model test suite in :core:model locks the recalibration-sensitive contracts shared by analysis, display, and explore voting. EmotionGroupAnchorTest locks the structural anchor-table invariants recalibrated against the library: auto anchors stay inside the V-A domain (±0.95), pairs keep ≥0.25 spacing, RAGE is the highest-arousal group, ABYSS lowest-valence, BRIGHT/LOVE the two most-positive, STILL lowest-arousal, the negative set is exactly {emo/躁/窒息}, WITTY stays excluded from automatic voting, and legacy curves vote against the legacy anchor table while a manual point uses the row's own coordinate system. EmotionGroupVoteOrderTest locks deterministic, process-stable vote ordering: ratio ties fall back to group declaration order (ordinal) which is independent of the anchor table, so recalibration never changes tied order. EmotionConfidenceTest locks confidence = the top vote share, computing it on the vocal-compensated curve with the row's own anchor table, low when votes spread or none vote, a hint only when spread and never for user-tagged/curve-less songs, and contradictory cold-warm tag lists as a distinct level.

The ratio and calibration suites in :core:model lock the word-share and read-derived-coordinate semantics used by explore voting and display. EmotionTagRatioTest locks that each word carries its share of the whole song (ratios sum to 1 when all pass the display threshold), sub-threshold tags are dropped, user-tagged words carry no ratio, ratios come from the compensated curve, and an empty curve yields none. EmotionVoteRatiosTest locks that explore voting uses the displayed distribution, not the full one: only dominant words get a vote, the vote set equals what the detail page shows, user-tagged words vote with full weight, and the gate defaults to the display gate. VocalCalibrationTest locks read-derived vocal compensation: instrumental songs get a constant valence shift, vocal songs and rows without vocalScore do not, only valence moves (never arousal), and SongEmotion exposes the compensated curve/valence. SongEmotionDerivedPointTest locks that user-calibration coordinates are derived (mean anchor of the tags within the row's own coordinate system) rather than stored, so stored coordinates are ignored and never go stale across rescans, and user-only rows derive with the current anchor table.

SongEmotionsRepositoryTest runs against a real Room in-memory DB (not a fake DAO, since the projection SQL itself is under test) and locks: the P0 light projection where getAll/observeAll omit embeddingB64 while upsert still persists it and single-row get still decodes it; upsert inheriting user tags so rescanning never swallows corrections; saveCorrection creating a user-only row for an unanalysed song and clearCorrection deleting it while keeping model data, persisting the userTagsEdited flag; correction coordinates being derived at read time rather than stored; curve round-tripping through flat JSON; and bulk read keeping vocalScore (a 2026-10-25 regression where the projection SQL omitted it, making list rows silently skip vocal compensation while detail rows applied it — a silent null field).
